source.title: Bayesian Natural Gradient Fine-Tuning of CLIP Models via Kalman Filtering
source.authors: Hossein Abdi; Ming-Fei Sun; Wei Pan

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports few-shot CLIP fine-tuning results on ID and distribution-shifted image datasets, a new setting for this claim. It does not test the claim's random-label memorization and natural-label generalization comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy after fine-tuning and OOD robustness under injected corrupted data. These results concern OOD transfer and downstream accuracy, not the training-versus-test gap on natural labels after fitting arbitrary labels. Its comparisons and ablations therefore do not test V1–V8. The stated performance values are not extracted as rows because none measures a behavior named by those versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates Kalman-based CLIP adaptation through ID/OOD classification accuracy and robustness to corrupted training data. None of its comparisons tests V1–V8. AdamW baselines versus Kalman adaptation do not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD; curvature arguments do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps. Original sources are cited for background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they present Kalman-based CLIP fine-tuning as approximating natural-gradient updates and achieving superior or comparable ID performance with improved OOD robustness. This describes their conclusion, although the reported superiority is not universal: ImageNet-A accuracy is below zero-shot CLIP and CoOp, and several ID settings favor other baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Bayesian Kalman-based adaptation of frozen CLIP backbones with trainable low-rank adapters; evaluates ID and OOD classification performance rather than arbitrary-label memorization and natural-label generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the OOD-data proportion and scaling factor α change robustness and training stability; forgetting factor β also changes test accuracy and may cause divergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Kalman-based few-shot CLIP adaptation achieves competitive ID accuracy and a Table II average accuracy of 48.93%, versus 47.99% for Tip-Adapter-F, across ImageNet and four shifted variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kalman-based adaptation can improve average classification accuracy across ID and distribution-shifted datasets relative to the tested CLIP adaptation baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: The benefit of scaling factor α depends on the proportion of corrupted training images; aggressive scaling can cause divergence at low corruption proportions. Forgetting factor β also affects accuracy and stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kalman-based CLIP adaptation depends on covariance-update and robustness hyperparameters, with their effectiveness varying across data conditions.

record.problems: The experiments use few-shot CLIP fine-tuning and report classification accuracy, not training error or the train-test gap. No uncertainty estimates for the reported accuracy values are given in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were eligible: the reported ID/OOD accuracy comparisons and α/β ablations do not measure any version's specified behavior. Values appear in Tables I–IV and Figures 2–3.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under comparable tuning, including training performance.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, dropout strength, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly stated gate note. Empty rows and verdicts are appropriate. The out-of-version results were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing eligible rows. Table II's average includes ID ImageNet as well as four OOD datasets.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or test-error analysis beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch generalization-gap analysis.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or comparison with random removals.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
